fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Assay card: measures receptor identities, usually by the complementarity-determining region 3 of the variable region, and their measured representation in the sampled population. How: extract nucleic acid, amplify or capture receptor regions, sequence, then group and count under stated rules, which may use nucleotide or amino-acid sequence, gene segments, one chain or paired chains. Input: blood cells or tissue nucleic acid for bulk methods and compatible cell preparations for single-cell methods, and preparation consumes material. A high-resolution human repertoire method reported chain diversity without sequence-associated or quantitative restrictions (Ruggiero 2015). Failure modes: poor material, shallow sampling, amplification bias, chain mismatch, inconsistent definitions and batch effects. It cannot tell every receptor's target, tissue position, killing or benefit, and a research method is not automatically a treatment-selection test.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Nucleotide and amino-acid clonotypes need not be the same grouping. The standard genetic code assigns several codons to the same amino acid, so different nucleotide sequences can encode the same receptor segment; amino-acid identity alone is not proof of one cellular lineage. MIGEC introduced molecular-identifier groups to correct PCR and sequencing errors in antibody and T-cell receptor repertoire profiling (Shugay 2014). Such error correction does not restore molecules absent from the sample. Report which chain, grouping rule and abundance unit the method actually used.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Frequency arithmetic, fictional: clonotype A is 10 of 10,000 sampled receptor units at baseline (0.1%) and 20 of 1,000 later (2%). The measured relative frequency rose twentyfold, but these are sampled receptor units and not a census of cells, and other populations contracting, different sampling and method effects can change frequency. Read counts are not always cell counts, because preparation, amplification and transcript abundance can change them, and absolute expansion needs compatible cell-number evidence. A sequence overlap between blood and tumour is detected overlap under a clonotype definition and is not a target, and antigen specificity needs a matching controlled recognition experiment.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: A repertoire report can give a clonotype list, relative frequencies, diversity, clonality and overlap, but there is no universal expansion or clonality threshold that proves tumour specificity. A sequence found in dissociated tumour material does not locate its cell inside a cancer-cell nest. Not detected means absent from the assay result under its sampling and calling rules, while an observed overlap or change nominates a receptor for a separate controlled recognition experiment.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: The usable input for a downstream assay is the recovered viable cell preparation, not simply the volume of blood drawn. Fresh isolation, freezing, thawing, washing and any rest period define a sequence of selections, so record recovery, population composition and purity as well as viability. The Cytiva density-separation handbook describes the mononuclear interface, platelet carryover and possible immature-granulocyte contamination in pathological blood. That manufacturer method source does not validate every cancer assay, and an inadequate number of the relevant cells can make a rare-response experiment uninformative.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: A stored PBMC sample is a finite specimen. It does not establish immune infiltration of a tumour, preserve every function or population equally, identify antigen specificity, or guarantee enough material for every later test. In the fictional equal-viability comparison, losing monocytes can affect a whole-protein stimulation because antigen-presenting-cell composition matters; viability alone does not establish interchangeable inputs. Fit and acceptance rules belong to the intended downstream assay.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Handling is evidence: in HIV vaccine assay studies, the time from venipuncture to cryopreservation was the most important parameter, and blood processed at 24 hours compared with within 8 hours lost on average about 8% of PBMC viability, about 32% of cell recovery and 36% to 56% of interferon gamma T-cell frequencies by ELISpot, which led the authors to recommend cryopreservation within 8 hours (Bull 2007). That is a finding for those protocols and assays and is not a universal schedule for cancer assays. A rapidly processed baseline and a delayed follow-up can therefore confound a biological comparison, and a high viability percentage alone does not show that every population or function was preserved.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Preparation card: input is anticoagulated blood or a blood-cell collection product and separation processes that aliquot and retains a selected cell fraction for compatible downstream assays. Output is recovered cell number, viable-cell percentage, recovery after thawing and measured population fractions, with cells per original blood volume needing a documented calculation. Controls are collection and processing timestamps, anticoagulant, storage, counting and viability methods and matched handling across time points. Thresholds are acceptance rules set for the intended downstream assay and not one universal quality number. Fictional case: two tubes have equally high viability but one recovered far fewer monocytes, so they are not automatically interchangeable for a whole-protein stimulation assay, because monocytes can contribute antigen presentation and viability does not show composition.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Denominators, fictional arithmetic: a run records 12,000 events, and after excluding debris, cell pairs and dead-cell events 10,000 recovered gated cells remain, of which 1,000 are T-cell events and 100 bind a reagent. Binding is 100 / 1,000 = 10% of the T-cell parent, 100 / 10,000 = 1% of recovered cells and 100 / 12,000 = 0.83% of recorded events. All three are correct for their own question and exchanging them changes the claim. Nested gates show membership and not area, no cells per millilitre or whole-body total follows, and binding or marker identity does not show killing.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: light scatter and fluorescence from individual events in a prepared cell suspension, grouped by a chosen panel of stains. Input: whole blood, isolated cells or dissociated tissue, where preparation and staining use a defined aliquot and compatibility with later assays depends on fixation and other processing and tissue dissociation removes geography and can recover cell types unevenly. Output: event counts, percent of a named parent population, fluorescence in instrument-dependent units, and cells per volume only with a validated counting method. Controls: instrument checks, unstained and single-stain controls, viability, biological controls and fluorescence-minus-one controls for hard boundaries. Failure modes: dead cells, aggregates, weak markers, nonspecific staining, signal overlap, cell loss and inconsistent gates. It cannot tell unmeasured proteins, original tissue position, antigen specificity from general markers or benefit.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Gating is selection within recorded data, not physical collection. A typical analysis checks acquisition quality, excludes debris and cell pairs, assesses viability where the assay requires it, and identifies populations with a stated marker panel. Intracellular assays may assess viability before fixation; not every flow experiment studies living cells. Fluorescence-minus-one controls omit one stain while retaining the others and can help place a boundary, but do not establish antibody specificity. Tight earlier gates can discard unexpected or rare populations. Automated clusters still need biological and technical checks (Cossarizza 2021). A cell sorter can physically collect selected events for downstream work, subject to recovery, purity and functional-viability requirements; an analytical gate alone does not do this (Cossarizza 2019).
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: What compensation does and does not do: in multicolour analysis spectral overlap between detectors needs compensation, and a mathematical and experimental analysis showed that photon-counting statistics add a nonlinear error to compensated parameters while measurement and log-scale binning errors add linear ones, most visibly with red and far-red fluorochromes where less light is emitted (Roederer 2001). Compensation or spectral unmixing therefore corrects overlap and does not repair a poorly chosen stain or set a positivity gate. The community guidelines (Cossarizza 2021) are methods guidance on preparation, panels and analysis and give no universal immune-response cut-off. A degranulation marker on the cell surface is an activity readout that accompanied cytolysis in antigen-specific CD8 T cells and is not itself measured target-cell death (Betts 2003).

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Scatter and marker panels help define populations under the stated assay, but scatter alone does not uniquely identify a cell type. Low event numbers and rare populations need uncertainty and acceptance rules appropriate to the panel and purpose. A gate boundary, minimum event count or research cluster is not a universal clinical-response threshold, and analytical reproducibility of the panel does not establish treatment benefit.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Absolute counts need a documented counting method, such as a suitable counting-bead standard or an instrument with validated absolute-count capability, with specimen volume and dilution retained. Counts of recorded events, percentages of a gate and cells per original blood volume are different outputs. The 2021 community guidelines describe both bead-based and instrument-based counting in specific protocols; neither makes every marker panel a validated clinical test.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Background arithmetic, fictional: matched wells of 100 identifiable targets show 30% death without effectors and 40% with them at the same 2-hour endpoint. Raw death is 40%, but 30% occurs without effectors, so the excess is 40 minus 30 = 10 percentage points. That excess is associated with the tested condition and does not identify which deaths the effectors caused, and calling the result 40% immune killing is not justified. A control-normalised specific-lysis formula gives a different quantity from an excess-death calculation, so the method has to be named, and a high baseline death can make the experiment unsuitable.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. A fall in a metabolic or growth signal can reflect slowed growth and not death, so it needs validation as evidence of killing. Controls: target-only survival wells, effector identification and viability, a positive-control response, irrelevant or antigen-negative targets and suitable antigen or presentation perturbations, plus maximum release where relevant. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Keep the identities and preparation of both effector and target cells, whether a cell line, engineered target or patient-derived preparation, together with medium, effector-to-target ratio and exposure time. Culture can change the tested population. The output might be a fraction of identified targets dead, a viable target count, release under a specified normalisation, or a time curve; these are different quantities. A negative is interpretable only when cell health, target suitability and controls support the experiment, and no universal laboratory killing cut-off establishes clinical efficacy. Reproducibility and biological specificity need checking for the specimen, model and intended claim.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: binding of cells to a specified peptide held by a specified HLA allele, under the staining conditions. How: HLA molecules are assembled with the selected peptide and several copies are attached to a labelled scaffold (a tetramer is one format), cells are exposed and analysed, usually by flow cytometry, with viable-cell and gate selection. Input: blood or tissue cells, where staining uses a defined aliquot and compatibility with later living-cell assays depends on the preparation, and the reagent must match both peptide and allele. Thresholds: gate and positivity rules need background and reagent controls, and no universal percentage shows efficacy. Failure modes: nonspecific binding, weak binding, dead cells, a wrong or poorly formed reagent, chain differences or sampling loss. It cannot tell cytokine response, tumour-cell killing, healthy-tissue specificity or benefit.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: What the evidence shows: in the original report, tetramers of HLA-A2 with two HIV-derived peptides or an influenza A matrix peptide bound peptide-specific cytotoxic T cells in vitro and T cells from the blood of HIV-infected people, and binding in general correlated well with cytotoxicity assays (Altman 1996). That is a correlation in those systems and not a rule that binding equals killing for an arbitrary tumour peptide. Tetramers are made by mixing biotinylated MHC with fluorescent streptavidin, and a later method made them with small-molecule fluorophores (Ramachandiran 2007), so reagent preparation is a source of variation. An observed stain shows binding under the tested conditions and does not show natural processing and display of that pair by a tumour.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Avidity describes the combined strength of multiple contacts. Multimerising peptide-HLA ligands can make binding detectable when an individual receptor-ligand contact is weak; the 2021 guidelines also caution that more multimerisation does not always improve detection. The measured output is a gate-defined binding fraction or, with a suitable counting method, a count. Reagent, viability and background controls support that binding measurement, which still requires separate validation before use for treatment selection.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Denominators, fictional arithmetic: 100 stained cells among 10,000 gated CD8 T cells is 1%, and the same 100 among 40,000 viable acquired cells is 0.25%. Both are correct and answer different denominator questions, and neither is a body-wide census or a killing rate. A tetramer-negative result is not a census of every possible relevant receptor, because some receptors bind too weakly for a given staining method, and HLA restriction belongs to the peptide-HLA pair and not the peptide alone.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Connecting assays is an inference task. A multimer-binding cell with no measured cytokine response need not identify one failed biological step: reagent performance, viability, stimulation, measurement window and each assay's threshold can differ. A cytokine response still does not directly measure target-cell death. Compatible cell sorting and receptor sequencing can connect binding to an operational receptor identity, but natural tumour presentation, recognition and killing remain separate questions to test.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: The stimulus changes the question. Added peptide can bypass some processing steps; whole protein needs suitable antigen-presenting cells and processing, while broad stimulation tests responsiveness without identifying the intended antigen. The 2021 flow-cytometry guidelines describe brefeldin A and monensin as transport inhibitors and explain that their choice and exposure window can affect what is measured. Intracellular accumulation after inhibition is not a measurement of how much cytokine reached the surrounding medium.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Fictional interpretation: a report finds cells positive for both interferon gamma and tumour necrosis factor after peptide stimulation. They are double-cytokine-positive under that assay and may not be called tumour-killing, because natural tumour recognition and death of appropriate targets need separate tests, and a strong response to a broad positive control confirms assay responsiveness and not recognition of the intended peptide. Polyfunctional means meeting the assay's rules for several measured functions, so it always needs its panel and stimulus attached, and a stained subset can contain many receptors.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Metrics and arithmetic, fictional: with natural logarithms Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times ln p, and one normalised clonality convention is 1 minus H / ln K for K observed clonotypes greater than one. Four clonotypes at 25, 25, 25 and 25 of 100 measured molecules give H = ln 4 = 1.386 and clonality 0. The same four at 70, 10, 10 and 10 give H = 0.940, clonality 1 minus 0.940 / 1.386 = 0.32, and an effective number of clonotypes exp(H) = 2.56. Richness is four in both, so many identities can coexist with strong dominance. Software may report Shannon entropy, its exponential or a normalised score, and these are not interchangeable: in the VDJtools documentation the Shannon-Wiener index returns the exponent of the entropy and the normalised index returns the entropy divided by the log of the clonotype count, which is evenness and not 1 minus that ratio, so a clonality built as 1 minus normalised entropy is a different number from either.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Effective-diversity measures weight a distribution differently. For the inverse-Simpson convention, define D as the sum of squared clonotype fractions and report 1 / D: four equal fractions of 0.25 give 4, whereas 0.70, 0.10, 0.10 and 0.10 give 1 / 0.52, about 1.92. This differs from the Shannon effective diversity of about 2.56 for the same uneven distribution. A fictional sample containing only A and B at 50 molecules each has richness 2 and equal weights; low richness does not imply unequal weights.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Share against count, fictional: clonotype A is 30 of 100 measured molecules, 30%, and later 30 of 50, 60%. Its measured count did not rise, the total fell, and its relative frequency doubled, so relative enrichment is not absolute expansion and the molecule counts are not blood cell counts. In a published analysis pipeline, clonality was identified as a robust key metric and first choice for measuring TCR repertoire diversity, and in prostate cancer patients given sipuleucel-T the pipeline detected changes in sequence frequency and diversity in blood and prostate tissue (Zhang 2017); that is a methods and example study and sets no response threshold. A diversity-analysis software suite reports repertoire comparison and diversity outputs (Shugay 2015), and formulas, software settings and subsampling depth have to be stated.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: The repertoire is a distribution of receptor identities and abundances in a stated population and time. A clone is a cellular lineage; a clonotype is an operational sequence grouping. Single-chain labels and paired identities have different resolution. V(D)J assembly and thymic selection contribute diversity, while expansion changes abundance; diversity and total T-cell count are different quantities.
fieldProofs.scope: Complete selected authored note read. This hash/containment check is distinct from the unit-specific semantic judgment and the named primary reading depth.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Measurement card: input is a sequencing-derived clonotype table and the calculation consumes no further tissue, though the upstream assay consumes its sample. Output units are a count for richness, dimensionless values for entropy and normalised clonality, and an effective clonotype count for effective diversity. Controls are matched compartments and handling, chain definition, error filtering, abundance units (reads, corrected molecules or cells are not automatically equivalent), depth assessment and replicates or resampling. Subsampling to a comparable depth helps assess sampling effects but cannot recover cells never sampled. A clonality summary does not identify what the receptors recognise, whether cells killed tumour, or whether treatment helped, and there is no universal clonality score that means an immune therapy is working.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: For one observed clonotype, the expression 1 minus H / ln K divides by ln 1, which is zero. Report how the software handles that case rather than silently applying the formula. Low input, unequal depth, amplification bias, sequence errors, changing mixtures and inconsistent clonotype definitions can alter the result. Keep the software version, formula, filtering, input, compartment and abundance units, and inspect the distribution alongside the summary. Analytical reproducibility of a repertoire statistic does not establish a prognostic association or predict treatment benefit.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Fictional arithmetic: wells with 100,000 input cells give 30 spots after peptide stimulation and 5 spots with vehicle. Background-subtracted, that is 30 minus 5 = 25 spots per 100,000 cells, or 250 spot-forming units per million input cells. This is an arithmetic summary and not a positivity cut-off, replicates, positive controls and a prespecified response rule still apply, and in mixed PBMCs it is not the frequency of a particular T-cell subset. If the cells came from an expanded culture, the number describes the cultured cells and not the responding fraction of the original blood draw.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: What the evidence does and does not support: the interferon gamma ELISpot is described as measuring the difference in the number of cells secreting the molecule with and without peptide, and interferon gamma is produced predominantly by natural killer and natural killer T cells as well as Th1 CD4 and CD8 effector T cells, so a mixed-cell spot does not by itself name the responding cell (Wykes and Renia protocol). In HIV vaccine research robust ELISpot responses were induced in a phase IIb trial that lacked efficacy, which challenged the assay's predictive power (Streeck 2009), and a validation in cynomolgus monkeys for responses to viral vector antigens (Yang 2022) validates that preparation and species and not cancer efficacy. Peptide added to cells can bypass the tumour's own processing and presentation, so a peptide response needs a separate bridge to natural tumour recognition.

fieldProofs.supportingExcerpt: Spot size or intensity is not a measure of target-cell killing. A negative result remains bounded by the number and condition of input cells, the stimulus, chosen secreted molecule, culture history and response rule; it is not a census of every responding cell in the body. Assay reproducibility and a cancer-treatment benefit claim need separate evidence.
